# The Bounded Observer

> A research programme derived from one premise: an observer with finite access, standing
> inside the world it measures. Finite access forces a predictive state; bounded quantities
> force a composition law; that law forces a horizon; the horizon forces a hyperbolic
> geometry. The central theorem is the Universal Hyperbolic Law. Author: Daniel John Murray,
> ORCID 0009-0005-1794-5945.

Every claim carries a status tag: [P] proven or classical with citation, [D] derived and
awaiting checking, [H] hypothesis with a stated test and a stated loss condition. Claims are
promoted only when a test has run. Refuted predictions are kept in the record.

## Start

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): rules for agents working here. Read before writing anything.
- [README.md](README.md): the programme on one page, and the six gates.

## The six gates, in order

- [1 Access](docs/1-access.md): what an observer can reach from inside.
- [2 State](docs/2-state.md): what must be kept so the rest of the past can be forgotten.
- [3 Action](docs/3-action.md): which interventions act the same way from every state.
- [4 Chart and boundary](docs/4-chart.md): how bounded changes combine; the horizon.
- [5 Geometry](docs/5-geometry.md): the shape of the room inside the horizon.
- [6 Prediction](docs/6-prediction.md): what has been tested, and what failed.

## Sources

- [papers/capstone/](papers/capstone/): Bounded Composition and Its Horizons, v2.1. Theorems
  are numbered; cite by number.
- [toolkit/](toolkit/): the Python package `bounded`. Each module names the theorem it
  implements; `pytest toolkit/tests` checks them numerically.
- [registry/atlas.csv](registry/atlas.csv): every work in the programme placed as a chart of
  the law, with its bounded quantity, its status and its next test.
- [experiments/](experiments/): pre-registered tests with data and code, including H1, which
  was refuted as stated.
- [apps/ida-live/](apps/ida-live/): IDA Live, the instrument that runs the law on a living mind.

## Optional

- [site/](site/): the website source; twelve interactive simulations, each tied to a theorem.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): how to add a chart, a replication or a refutation.
